mainTopic: The four women who are דיין שעתן, and שמואל's list of cases where the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about four women (בתולה, מעוברת, מניקה, זקנה) who are טמא only from the moment they see blood (דיה שעתה). The משנה rules like רבי אליעזר and defines each of the four women. It also brings a מחלוקת about a mother who stopped nursing and wider views from רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי. It then limits the leniency to the first sighting, unless that first sighting came from an אונס. The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר tells רבי יהושע that he heard the tradition about many women. It explains why people followed רבי יהושע while רבי אליעזר was alive: רבי אליעזר was a שמותי, and out of respect for him no one could protest if people followed his other rulings. Then שמואל lists four cases where the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר, including the impure outsides of vessels, along with a debate about a קל וחומר from a טבול יום. The גמרא explains that שמואל teaches that we do not decide הלכה only from a ruling written in a משנה or ברייתא. Finally it asks whether his list is complete, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: After רבי יהושע says he only heard the rule about a בתולה, the משנה rules that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר's list of four women.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the הלכה is like רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: After the debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, the משנה gives the final ruling: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר, so all four women get דיה שעתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע had a tradition only about a בתולה, so his view was narrower. The משנה rules for the wider list of רבי אליעזר. That fixes the practical rule before the משנה goes on to define each woman.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
Her time is enough: she is טמא only from the moment she sees blood, not backwards

steps.whyThisMatters: Because the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר, all the definitions that follow matter in practice for all four women.

phrases.english: But the halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous part of the משנה (the debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All four women (בתולה, מעוברת, מניקה, זקנה) are דיין שעתן.

steps.title: Who counts as a virgin
steps.stepSummary: A בתולה here is any woman who has never had a period, even if she is married.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is a 'virgin'? Any woman who has never seen menstrual blood in her life, even if she is married.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts defining the four women, beginning with the בתולה. Here the word means a woman who has never had a period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בתולה here does not mean what it usually means. It is about whether she has ever menstruated. So a married woman who has never had a period still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a woman who has never had a period
In all her days, ever in her life

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read בתולה as 'unmarried' or 'never had relations.' In this משנה it only means she has never menstruated.

phrases.english: Who is a 'virgin'?
Any woman who has not seen blood in all her days,
even though she is married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר, the משנה defines the first of his four women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בתולה is a woman who has never menstruated, even if she is married.

steps.title: When pregnancy and nursing begin and end
steps.stepSummary: A pregnant woman gets the leniency once her pregnancy is noticeable. A nursing woman gets it until she weans her child.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pregnant woman: from when her pregnancy is known. A nursing woman: until she weans her child.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets the time span for the מעוברת and the מניקה. It says when each of them has the status of דיה שעתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a pregnant woman, the status begins only once the pregnancy can be recognized, not from conception. For a nursing woman, it lasts as long as she is nursing and ends when she weans.

keyTerms.meaning: From when her fetus becomes known (the pregnancy is noticeable)

phrases.english: A pregnant woman: from when her fetus is known.
A nursing woman: until she weans her child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues defining the four women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעוברת: from when the pregnancy is known. מניקה: until weaning.

steps.title: A nursing mother who stopped nursing
steps.stepSummary: Suppose a woman stopped nursing during the nursing period: she gave the baby to a wet nurse, weaned him, or the baby died. רבי מאיר says she is טמא backwards 24 hours. חכמים say she still gets דיה שעתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she gave her child to a wet nurse, weaned him, or he died: רבי מאיר says she is impure for the past 24 hours, and the חכמים say her time is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a מחלוקת about a mother who is no longer actually nursing, though she is still within the nursing period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that once she has actually stopped nursing, she loses the leniency and is treated like any other woman (מעת לעת). חכמים hold that she keeps the status of a מניקה even though she is not nursing now.

keyTerms.meaning: She makes things טמא backwards for a 24-hour period

phrases.english: If she gave her child to a wet nurse,
weaned him, or he died,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: מְטַמְּאָה מֵעֵת לְעֵת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: she transmits impurity for a twenty-four-hour period,
and the Sages say: her time is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the edge of the מניקה definition: what if she stopped nursing early?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: מעת לעת. חכמים: דיה שעתה.

steps.title: Who counts as an elderly woman
steps.stepSummary: A זקנה is a woman near old age who has gone three cycles without a period.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is an 'elderly woman'? Any woman who has gone three cycles without bleeding, close to her old age.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines the last of the four women, the זקנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Age alone is not enough. She must be close to old age and must also have gone three עונות without seeing blood. Both conditions are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Cycles: the usual time spans between periods

phrases.english: Who is an 'elderly woman'?
Any woman for whom three cycles have passed
phrases.notes: He means three cycles went by without her seeing any blood.

phrases.english: close to her old age.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of four definitions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זקנה is a woman near old age who has missed three עונות.
steps.whatToRemember: The four women: בתולה (never had a period), מעוברת (pregnancy noticeable), מניקה (until weaning), זקנה (near old age with three missed cycles).

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: any woman who missed three cycles
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר widens the rule. Any woman, at any age, who went three cycles without a period gets דיה שעתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: any woman who has gone three cycles without bleeding, her time is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the age condition in the previous definition. For him, missing three cycles is enough by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous definition needed both old age and three missed cycles. רבי אליעזר drops the age requirement. The missed cycles alone show that her bleeding has stopped, so she gets the leniency.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ שָׁלֹשׁ עוֹנוֹת —
phrases.english: any woman for whom three cycles have passed,
her time is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ שָׁלֹשׁ עוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the זקנה definition by removing the age condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three missed עונות are enough for any woman to be דיה שעתה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי on pregnant and nursing women
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי speaks about pregnant and nursing women who went three cycles without blood: they are דיין שעתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: a pregnant woman and a nursing woman who have gone three cycles without bleeding, their time is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds another view. He applies the 'three cycles' idea to pregnant and nursing women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי brings the three missed עונות into the cases of the מעוברת and the מניקה. That is a different focus from the earlier definitions, which set their status by noticeable pregnancy and by weaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Their time is enough (plural form of דיה שעתה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
a pregnant woman and a nursing woman
for whom three cycles have passed,
their time is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another opinion that uses the three-cycles idea, here for מעוברת and מניקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מעוברת or מניקה who went three עונות without blood is דיין שעתן.

steps.title: When does 'her time is enough' apply?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks which sightings of blood the leniency of דיה שעתה covers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in what case did they say 'her time is enough'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The משנה asks a question so it can limit the leniency in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the משנה only said who gets דיה שעתה. Now it asks whether the leniency covers every sighting of blood or only some of them.

keyTerms.meaning: And in what case did he say? (a question that sets limits)

phrases.english: And in what case did he say 'her time is enough'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who gets the leniency to how far it reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does דיה שעתה apply to every sighting, or only some?

steps.title: Only the first sighting is lenient
steps.stepSummary: דיה שעתה applies only to the first time she sees blood. From the second time on, she is treated like any woman (מעת לעת).
steps.simpleTranslation: With the first sighting; but with the second, she is impure for the past 24 hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question: the leniency covers only the first sighting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she has seen blood, she is no longer clearly 'not bleeding.' So after that first time she loses her special status. At the second sighting she becomes טמא backwards מעת לעת like everyone else.

phrases.english: With the first sighting;
but with the second, she transmits impurity for a twenty-four-hour period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the first sighting is דיה שעתה. The second is מעת לעת.

steps.title: If the first sighting came from an outside cause
steps.stepSummary: If the first blood came from an אונס (an outside cause), it does not count. So even the second sighting is still דיה שעתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she saw the first one because of an outside cause, even the second is 'her time is enough.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה makes an exception to the rule it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood that came from an אונס does not show that her natural bleeding has returned. So the first sighting does not take away her status. The next sighting is treated as her real 'first,' and she still gets דיה שעתה.

keyTerms.meaning: An outside cause, something forced on her, not her natural cycle

steps.whatToRemember: דיה שעתה covers only the first natural sighting. A sighting caused by אונס does not use up the leniency.

phrases.english: And if she saw the first one because of an outside cause,
even the second, her time is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the 'first sighting only' rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A first sighting caused by אונס does not count, so the next sighting is still דיה שעתה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: I heard more than you did
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי אליעזר telling רבי יהושע that his tradition covers many women, not just one, and compares this to witnesses for the new moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי אליעזר said to רבי יהושע: You did not hear this, but I did. You heard about only one case, and I heard about many. We don't tell someone who never saw the new moon to come and testify. We tell that only to the one who saw it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר answers רבי יהושע's claim from the משנה that he heard the rule only about a בתולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע said he only received the tradition of דיה שעתה for a בתולה. רבי אליעזר answers that not having heard something proves nothing, because he did hear it, and about many women. Like testimony about the new moon, the person who actually saw something is the one whose word counts.

keyTerms.meaning: I heard, meaning I received a tradition from my teachers
The new moon, which witnesses saw and reported to בית דין

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua:
You did not hear, but I heard;
phrases.notes: He is answering רבי יהושע's words in the משנה, that he heard the rule only about a בתולה.

phrases.english: you heard only one,
and I heard many.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְרִים לְמִי שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: We do not say to one who did not see the new moon
"Let him come and testify," but only to one who saw it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by bringing a ברייתא about the מחלוקת in the משנה between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A positive tradition from one who heard outweighs the silence of one who did not hear.

steps.title: What people actually did, before and after רבי אליעזר's passing
steps.stepSummary: During רבי אליעזר's life the practice followed רבי יהושע. After he passed away, רבי יהושע restored the earlier practice, which followed רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the days of רבי אליעזר, people acted like רבי יהושע. After רבי אליעזר passed away, רבי יהושע returned the matter to how it used to be.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reports the history of how people practiced. Under רבי יהושע they followed him while רבי אליעזר lived, and afterward they went back to רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising. רבי יהושע himself is the one who switched the practice to his opponent's view. This sets up the question in the next step: if רבי אליעזר's view was right, why wasn't it followed while he was alive?

keyTerms.meaning: Acting in practice according to someone's view

steps.confusionAlert: "Returned the matter to its former state" does not mean returning to רבי יהושע's view. It means going back to the original practice, which was רבי אליעזר's view.

phrases.english: All the days of Rabbi Eliezer
they would act in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua;
after Rabbi Eliezer's passing,

phrases.aramaic: הֶחְזִיר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶת הַדָּבָר לְיוֹשְׁנוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua returned the matter to its former state.
phrases.notes: The former state was following רבי אליעזר, so רבי יהושע brought back his opponent's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא by reporting how the practice was actually carried out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, the הלכה followed רבי אליעזר after his passing, through רבי יהושע's own decision.

steps.title: Why not follow רבי אליעזר during his lifetime?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר's view was not followed while he was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why didn't they act like רבי אליעזר while he was alive?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the story it just told. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהושע himself later restored רבי אליעזר's view, he clearly thought it was correct. So why wait until after רבי אליעזר's passing?

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, during his lifetime,
what is the reason they did not?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, בְּחַיָּיו מַאי טַעְמָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the practice described in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אליעזר's correct view was not practiced while he was alive.

steps.title: Because רבי אליעזר followed בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר was a שמותי. The concern was that following him on one point would lead people to follow him on other points too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because רבי אליעזר was a שמותי, and the thinking was: if we act like him on one thing, people will act like him on other things too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי אליעזר generally held like בית שמאי, so following him even once was risky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the הלכה follows בית הלל, not בית שמאי. If people saw רבי אליעזר's view practiced in this case, they might start following his other rulings, where the הלכה is not like him.

keyTerms.meaning: A follower of בית שמאי's rulings

phrases.english: Because Rabbi Eliezer is a Shammuti,
and the thinking was: if we act like him in one matter,
we will act like him in other matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Following a שמותי on one point could lead people to follow him on all his points.

steps.title: Respect for רבי אליעזר made protest impossible until he passed away
steps.stepSummary: While רבי אליעזר lived, his honor prevented anyone from protesting against people who followed his other rulings. After his passing protest became possible, so the practice was restored.
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of רבי אליעזר's honor, we could not protest against them. After רבי אליעזר passed away, when we could protest against them, he returned the matter to how it used to be.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer. It explains why the worry existed only during רבי אליעזר's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger was not only that people might follow him elsewhere. While he was alive, respect for him meant no one could stop them. Once he passed away, people who wrongly followed his other rulings could be corrected, so the correct practice here could safely return.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה in this case follows רבי אליעזר. It was held back during his life only because of the fear that people would follow his בית שמאי rulings, and no one could protest out of respect for him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a correct ruling can be delayed in practice for wider communal reasons, without changing what the הלכה really is.

phrases.english: And because of the honor of Rabbi Eliezer,
we would not be able to protest against them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means people who follow רבי אליעזר's other rulings.

phrases.english: After Rabbi Eliezer's passing,
when we are able to protest against them,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the word in square brackets. Both mean "we are able."

phrases.english: he returned the matter to its former state.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, לָא מָצֵינַן מָחֵינַן בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous step and explains why things changed after רבי אליעזר's passing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Respect for רבי אליעזר blocked any protest while he lived. After his passing protest was possible, so his view here was restored.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practice follows רבי אליעזר, and it was delayed only to prevent people from following his other בית שמאי rulings.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי אליעזר in four cases
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in four cases. The first is the case already discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in four cases. One of them is the case we just talked about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a list of four places where we rule like רבי אליעזר. It names the first one and sets up the next cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר is usually not followed in practice, so a list of exceptions is worth noting. The first case is the one from the earlier steps: certain women are impure only from the time they see blood, and not before.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion
One (the first item in a list)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the גמרא keeps going with a list of rulings. It is collecting the rare cases where רבי אליעזר's view is the law.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer in four cases.
One: the one we already said.
phrases.notes: He means the case we just learned: the women who are impure only from the moment they see blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of the practice going back to רבי אליעזר, the גמרא brings a broader list of cases where the הלכה follows him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in four cases. The first is the one already discussed.

steps.title: Second case: a woman in hard labor who gets relief
steps.stepSummary: A woman bleeding during hard labor becomes a זבה only if she had a full twenty-four hours of relief from the pain. This is רבי אליעזר's view, and the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second case: a woman in hard labor. How long must she have relief from the pain to be counted as a זבה? A full twenty-four hours. These are the words of רבי אליעזר, and the הלכה follows him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second of the four cases where we follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood that comes with labor pain is treated as birth blood, not as זיבה. If the pain stopped for a full day before the bleeding, the blood is no longer tied to the birth, so she can become a זבה. The source states clearly that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר here.

keyTerms.meaning: And another one (the next item in the list)
A woman having hard, painful labor
Get relief, be calm from the pain
A woman made impure by bleeding outside her normal time

phrases.english: And another:
A woman in hard labor: how long must she have relief from the pain
phrases.notes: Blood during labor pain counts as birth blood. The question is how long the pain must stop before the blood counts as זיבה.

phrases.english: and be a zava?
For a full twenty-four-hour period,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer,
and the halacha follows his words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second item in שמואל's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman in labor needs twenty-four hours of relief from the pain before her bleeding makes her a זבה. The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Third case: checking only on the first and seventh days
steps.stepSummary: A זב or זבה checked themselves on day one and day seven of the seven clean days and found themselves pure, but did not check on the days in between. רבי אליעזר says they are presumed pure. רבי יהושע says only days one and seven count. רבי עקיבא says only day seven counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The third case: a זב or זבה checked themselves on the first day and were pure, and on the seventh day and were pure, but did not check on the other days. רבי אליעזר says they are presumed pure. רבי יהושע says they have only the first and seventh days. רבי עקיבא says they have only the seventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the third case on the list by quoting a three-way argument. This sets up the next step, which tells us whose view is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב or זבה must count seven clean days. רבי אליעזר assumes the unchecked days were clean, so the count is complete. רבי יהושע counts only the days that were actually checked. רבי עקיבא goes further: if there had been a flow in between, the count would restart, so only the last day is certain.

keyTerms.meaning: A man made impure by an unusual discharge

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא do not say the person is impure forever. They are arguing about how many of the seven clean days were counted, so the person must count the missing days again.

phrases.english: And another:
A zav and a zava who checked themselves
on the first day and found themselves pure,
on the seventh day and found themselves pure,
but on the rest of the days they did not check:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
they are presumed pure.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
they have counted only the first day
and the seventh day alone.
Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶם אֶלָּא יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: they have counted only the seventh day alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the third item in שמואל's list. It gives the argument before the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: presumed pure. רבי יהושע: only days one and seven count. רבי עקיבא: only day seven counts.

steps.title: A ברייתא rules like רבי אליעזר in the זב case
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון and רבי יוסי say that רבי עקיבא's reasoning seems the strongest, and רבי אליעזר's seems stronger than רבי יהושע's. Even so, they say the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון and רבי יוסי say that רבי אליעזר's view seems better than רבי יהושע's, and רבי עקיבא's view seems better than all of them. But the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in the case of the זב and זבה. That is why this case belongs on שמואל's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first ranks the opinions by how strong their reasoning seems, and it puts רבי עקיבא on top. Still, it rules in practice like רבי אליעזר. This shows that the opinion that sounds most logical is not always the one we follow.
steps.whatToRemember: So far, three of the four cases where the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר: (1) the case already discussed, (2) a woman in labor needs a full day of relief before she can become a זבה, and (3) a זב or זבה who checked only on days one and seven is presumed pure.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying an opinion 'seems more correct' is not the same as ruling like it. Here רבי עקיבא's view seems strongest, but the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yosei say:
The words of Rabbi Eliezer seem more correct
than the words of Rabbi Yehoshua,
and the words of Rabbi Akiva seem more correct than the words of all of them,
but the halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It gives the source for ruling like רבי אליעזר in the argument quoted in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in the case of the זב and זבה, which makes it the third item on שמואל's list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון and רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The case of vessel outsides made impure by liquids
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the next case on שמואל's list, a משנה about the outsides of vessels that became impure through liquids. רבי אליעזר says they make liquids impure but do not disqualify foods. רבי יהושע says they do both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other case is the one we learned in a משנה: If the outsides of vessels became impure through liquids, רבי אליעזר says they make liquids impure but do not disqualify foods. They make liquids impure, even non-sacred ones. They do not disqualify foods, even תרומה. רבי יהושע says they make liquids impure and they also disqualify foods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case where the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר. It quotes a משנה where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about what impure vessel outsides can make impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages agree that these vessel outsides make liquids impure. They argue only about foods. רבי אליעזר goes far in both directions: even ordinary liquids become impure, and even holy תרומה food is not disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: They disqualify (make something unfit, without passing impurity further)
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which has extra holiness

steps.confusionAlert: The two sides do not argue about liquids at all. Both say liquids become impure. The whole argument is only about foods.

phrases.english: And the other one, as we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This is the next case on שמואל's list of rulings that follow רבי אליעזר (step 16).

phrases.english: The outsides of vessels that became impure through liquids,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
They make liquids impure
but they do not disqualify foods.
They make liquids impure, even non-sacred ones,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין פּוֹסְלִין אֶת הָאֳוכָלִין, וַאֲפִילּוּ דִּתְרוּמָה.
phrases.english: and they do not disqualify foods, even foods of teruma.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַמַּשְׁקִין וּפוֹסְלִין אֶת הָאֳוכָלִין.
phrases.english: They make liquids impure and they also disqualify foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in שמואל's list of four rulings that follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessel outsides made impure by liquids make liquids impure. רבי אליעזר says they do not disqualify foods. רבי יהושע says they do.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's קל וחומר from a טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע proves his view with a קל וחומר. A טבול יום cannot make ordinary liquids impure, yet he disqualifies תרומה food. Vessel outsides can make ordinary liquids impure, so surely they disqualify תרומה food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: This is a קל וחומר. A טבול יום does not make ordinary liquids impure, yet he disqualifies תרומה food. Vessel outsides do make ordinary liquids impure. Isn't it logical that they disqualify תרומה food?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives the reason for his view. He uses a קל וחומר, a 'how much more so' argument, comparing vessel outsides to a טבול יום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טבול יום is the 'weaker' case, since he cannot even make ordinary liquids impure, yet he still disqualifies תרומה food. Vessel outsides are 'stronger', since they do make ordinary liquids impure. So they should at least do what the weaker case does and disqualify תרומה food.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument: if the weaker case has a rule, the stronger case surely has it
Someone who immersed in a מקוה today and is waiting for nightfall to become fully pure
Isn't it logical? (the closing words of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said: It is an a fortiori argument,
if one who immersed that day,
who does not make non-sacred liquids impure,
still disqualifies teruma foods,
then the outsides of vessels, which do make non-sacred liquids impure,
isn't it logical that they disqualify teruma foods?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי יהושע's view in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע's ruling that vessel outsides disqualify תרומה food
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the law of a טבול יום

steps.title: Why רבי אליעזר rejects the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר's answer. Vessel outsides are impure only by rabbinic law, while a טבול יום is Torah law. We do not use a קל וחומר to learn a rabbinic rule from a Torah law. By Torah law, food and liquid cannot make a vessel impure at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר? Vessel outsides are a rabbinic rule, and a טבול יום is Torah law. We do not make a קל וחומר from Torah law to rabbinic law. By Torah law, food does not make a vessel impure, and liquid does not make a vessel impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר deals with רבי יהושע's קל וחומר, and answers that the comparison does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר works only between cases of the same kind. The טבול יום rule comes from the Torah. The impurity of vessel outsides is only a rabbinic decree, since by Torah law liquids cannot make a vessel impure in the first place. So the Torah rule cannot teach us how far the rabbinic decree reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: A law made by the חכמים (rabbinic law)
A law from the Torah itself
We do not make a קל וחומר

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a general rule: you cannot use a קל וחומר to stretch a rabbinic law based on a Torah law.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer, how does he answer this?
The outsides of vessels are impure by rabbinic law,
and one who immersed that day is a Torah law,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא עָבְדִינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר,
phrases.english: and we do not make an a fortiori argument to rabbinic law from Torah law,
since by Torah law food does not make a vessel impure,
and liquid does not make a vessel impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהושע's קל וחומר on behalf of רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from טבול יום to vessel outsides
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It learns a rabbinic rule from a Torah law, and a קל וחומר does not work across that line.

steps.title: Why the חכמים decreed on liquids but not on foods
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים made this decree because of the liquids of a זב and זבה. Since liquids pick up impurity easily, the decree covered them. Foods do not pick up impurity as easily, so the decree did not cover them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was the חכמים who made a decree, because of the liquids of a זב and זבה. Liquids, which easily pick up impurity, the חכמים included in their decree. Foods, which do not easily pick up impurity, the חכמים did not include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where this rabbinic decree came from. It also explains why, by רבי אליעזר's view, it covers only liquids and not foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree was made because liquids that come from a זב or זבה really can make vessels impure, and people might confuse them with other liquids. Since this was only a rabbinic decree, the חכמים limited it. They applied it to liquids, which pick up impurity easily, and not to foods, which do not.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree made by the חכמים
A man or woman with an impure discharge, whose body fluids are a source of impurity
Likely to pick up impurity easily

steps.whatToRemember: By רבי אליעזר, and the הלכה follows him: vessel outsides make liquids impure but never disqualify foods, even תרומה. The decree is rabbinic, so a Torah-based קל וחומר cannot expand it.

phrases.english: And it was the Sages who made a decree,
because of the liquids of a zav and zava,
liquids, which easily pick up impurity —
the Sages decreed about them,
foods, which do not easily pick up impurity —
the Sages did not decree about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the point that the impurity is rabbinic and explains the source and limits of the decree.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The decree on vessel outsides was made because of the liquids of a זב and זבה. It covers liquids, which easily pick up impurity, but not foods.

steps.title: Why did he single out vessel outsides?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר's ruling is framed around the outsides of vessels specifically.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about the outsides of vessels, that he chose to mention them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: why did רבי אליעזר talk specifically about the outsides of vessels? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said vessel outsides made impure by liquids do not disqualify food. The גמרא wants to know why the case is limited to the outside of a vessel and not the whole vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this case and not another?

phrases.english: And what is different about the outsides of vessels, that he mentioned them?
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי אליעזר, whose ruling about vessel outsides we just learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the reason for the decree on liquids, the גמרא asks why the ruling is about vessel outsides in particular.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אליעזר's ruling is limited to the outsides of vessels.

steps.title: Vessel outsides are a lighter impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that vessel outsides are treated more leniently, and proves it from a משנה: impurity on the outside stays on the outside, but impurity on the inside spreads to the whole vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are lenient. As we learned in a משנה: If a vessel's outside became impure through liquids, its outside is impure, but its inside, its ear, its rim, and its handles are pure. If its inside became impure, the whole vessel is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the outsides of vessels are a lighter level of impurity. It quotes a משנה to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that when the outside of a vessel becomes impure, the impurity stays on the outside only. When the inside becomes impure, the whole vessel becomes impure. Since the outside is already treated leniently, רבי אליעזר could also say it does not disqualify food.

keyTerms.meaning: They are lenient, a lighter level

steps.whatToRemember: Impurity on a vessel's outside stays on the outside, while impurity on the inside makes the whole vessel impure. That is why vessel outsides get a more lenient ruling.

phrases.english: Because they are lenient,
as we learned: a vessel whose outside became impure through liquids —
its outside is impure,
its inside, its ear, its rim, its handles are pure.
If its inside became impure, all of it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Vessel outsides are a lenient category, as the משנה shows that their impurity does not spread to the rest of the vessel.

steps.title: What does שמואל add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling: in all these cases the sources already state the הלכה, so what new thing is he teaching?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is שמואל teaching us? In all of these cases we already learned the הלכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to שמואל, who said the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in these cases. It asks why he needed to say this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sources themselves already say the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in these cases, as we saw with רבי שמעון and רבי יוסי. If so, שמואל's ruling seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? What is new here?

phrases.english: What is שמואל teaching us?
In all of them we learned the halacha!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the content of the cases to the purpose of שמואל's ruling about them.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in these cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sources already state the הלכה in each case, so שמואל's statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that שמואל means only vessel outsides
steps.stepSummary: One might say שמואל needed to rule on vessel outsides, where no הלכה was stated. The גמרא rejects this: then he should have said only that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that he is teaching us about vessel outsides, where we did not learn the הלכה, then let him just say: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר about vessel outsides!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible answer and then pushes it away right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For vessel outsides, the משנה never said who the הלכה follows, so שמואל's ruling would be new there. But then שמואל should have ruled only on that case. Listing all the cases means he is teaching something about all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (a suggested answer)

phrases.english: And if you will say,
he is teaching us about vessel outsides,
which we did not learn,
phrases.notes: The משנה about vessel outsides never said who the הלכה follows.

phrases.english: then let him say the halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer
regarding vessel outsides!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא, אֲחוֹרֵי כֵלִים קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and rejects one possible answer to the question of step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that שמואל's point was only about vessel outsides.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If that were his point, he would have ruled on that case alone and not listed all the cases.

steps.title: A written ruling alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שמואל teaches a general rule: we do not decide practical הלכה only from a ruling written in a משנה or ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he teaches us: we do not learn the הלכה from the mouth of the תלמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real answer: שמואל is teaching a general rule about how we decide הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when a משנה or ברייתא says 'the הלכה follows so-and-so,' that alone is not enough to rule in practice. A later teacher like שמואל has to confirm it. So שמואל's ruling is needed even in the cases where the source already gave the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not decide practical הלכה only from a ruling stated in a learned text
Here: the learned text itself, such as a משנה or ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's list is not extra. It teaches that a ruling written in a משנה or ברייתא needs confirmation before we rely on it in practice.
steps.confusionAlert: 'תלמוד' here does not mean our גמרא. It means the learned text, like a משנה or ברייתא, that states 'the הלכה follows so-and-so.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of how הלכה is decided: a statement inside a source is not enough by itself; it needs a later ruling.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he teaches us,
that we do not learn the halacha from the mouth of the learning.
phrases.notes: He means a line like 'the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר' inside a משנה or ברייתא is not enough by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the answer in step 27, gives the real answer to step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the statement as a general rule about deciding הלכה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's ruling seemed to repeat what the sources already said.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל teaches that a ruling stated in a משנה or ברייתא is not enough to decide practical הלכה without confirmation.

steps.title: Is שמואל's list complete?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's list: there seems to be another משנה where the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר, and it starts to quote it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there nothing more? But there is a case that we learned: רבי אליעזר says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether שמואל's list really has every case, and begins quoting another משנה. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gave a fixed number of cases. The גמרא suggests there is another case with רבי אליעזר that should also be on the list.

phrases.english: And is there no more?
But there is what we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in יבמות 109a.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
phrases.notes: The quote stops here; his words continue on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the purpose of שמואל's list, the גמרא questions whether the list is complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of שמואל's list of cases where the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה seems to have the הלכה following רבי אליעזר, so it should have been on the list.
